0.name: Apple Scab
0.description: Fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis leading to dark scabby lesions on leaves and fruit.

solution.immediate_action: Prune and destroy infected leaves and twigs; avoid overhead irrigation.
solution.organic: Apply liquid copper soap, wettable sulfur, or Bacillus subtilis sprays during bud break.
solution.chemical: Apply protective fungicides containing Captan, Mancozeb, or Difenoconazole at 7-10 day intervals.
solution.cultural: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn; prune tree canopy to optimize airflow and sunlight.

1.name: Apple Black Rot
symptoms: Frog-eye leaf spots with purple margins
1.description: Caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa, causing defoliation and severe fruit rotting.

solution.immediate_action: Remove mummified fruit and prune out cankered twigs 6-8 inches below visible damage.
solution.organic: Apply copper octanoate or sulfur fungicides during dormancy and early leaf development.
solution.chemical: Spray Captan or Thiophanate-methyl starting at petal fall through summer cover sprays.
solution.cultural: Disinfect pruning shears with 70% alcohol between cuts; burn or bury infected debris.

2.name: Apple Cedar Apple Rust
2.description: Fungal disease caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae cycling between apples and eastern red cedars.

solution.immediate_action: Scout for nearby Eastern Red Cedar trees harboring galls and prune affected apple foliage.
solution.organic: Apply sulfur or copper-based sprays every 7-10 days from tight cluster until petal fall.
solution.chemical: Apply Myclobutanil, Mancozeb, or Propiconazole before anticipated spring rainfall events.
solution.cultural: Eradicate wild cedar and juniper trees within 500 feet of the orchard where feasible.

3.name: Apple Healthy
3.description: Healthy apple foliage with high photosynthetic activity and zero disease symptoms.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Maintain balanced foliar nutrition and organic compost mulching.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Continue routine scouting, balanced drip irrigation, and annual winter pruning.

4.name: Blueberry Healthy
4.description: Healthy blueberry foliage ready for high berry yields.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Maintain acidic soil mulch (pine needles/peat moss) and organic fertilizer.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Maintain soil pH between 4.5 - 5.5 and ensure consistent root zone moisture.

5.name: Cherry Powdery Mildew
5.description: Caused by Podosphaera clandestina, damaging foliage and young developing cherries.

solution.immediate_action: Prune out dense shoot tips showing white fungal mildew to increase air penetration.
solution.organic: Spray potassium bicarbonate, neem oil, or horticultural oils in early morning.
solution.chemical: Apply Myclobutanil, Triflumizole, or Tebuconazole fungicide at first sign of white mycelium.
solution.cultural: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which promotes lush, susceptible succulent growth.

6.name: Cherry Healthy
6.description: Healthy cherry tree leaves with balanced canopy development.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Maintain good orchard sanitation and organic micronutrient sprays.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Monitor weekly for aphids and fruit flies; maintain weed-free tree understoreys.

7.name: Corn Gray Leaf Spot
7.description: Destructive foliar fungal disease caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis reducing kernel fill.

solution.immediate_action: Assess lower canopy leaf lesions before tasseling to determine economic spray threshold.
solution.organic: Apply Bacillus pumilus bio-fungicides and silicon-based foliar strengthening agents.
solution.chemical: Apply Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole or Pyraclostrobin at first appearance of gray lesions.
solution.cultural: Rotate fields with non-host crops (soybean/sunflower); plow under previous crop residues.

8.name: Corn Common Rust
8.description: Fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi, thriving in cool, moist weather and high humidity.

solution.immediate_action: Inspect leaf surfaces for cinnamon-brown pustules, especially under cool, humid conditions.
solution.organic: Spray sulfur-based protectants or Trichoderma harzianum bio-agents.
solution.chemical: Apply Propiconazole, Tebuconazole, or Pyraclostrobin if pustules reach ear leaves before silking.
solution.cultural: Plant rust-resistant hybrids; maintain balanced phosphorus and potassium fertilization.

9.name: Corn Northern Leaf Blight
symptoms: Lesions turning dark with fungal spores
9.description: Caused by Setosphaeria turcica, causing substantial loss in grain and silage corn yields.

solution.immediate_action: Scout ear leaf and two leaves below for large cigar-shaped lesions during pre-tassel stage.
solution.organic: Apply copper oxychloride or bio-fungicides containing Bacillus subtilis.
solution.chemical: Apply Strobilurin or Triazole fungicides (e.g. Azoxystrobin, Propiconazole) at early lesion detection.
solution.cultural: Incorporate corn stubble thoroughly; adopt a 2-year crop rotation with non-cereal crops.

10.name: Corn Healthy
10.description: Healthy vigorous corn foliage supporting optimal cob development.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Apply bio-fertilizers (Azotobacter, PSB) and organic soil amendments.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Maintain optimal planting density and adequate nitrogen side-dressing.

11.name: Grape Black Rot
11.description: Severe fungal disease caused by Guignardia bidwellii affecting vineyard canopies.

solution.immediate_action: Hand-pick and destroy mummified grapes and infected canes from previous season.
solution.organic: Apply copper octanoate or sulfur dusts from budbreak through bloom stage.
solution.chemical: Apply Mancozeb, Captan, or Myclobutanil starting at 1-3 inch shoot growth.
solution.cultural: Open grapevine canopies by shoot thinning to promote rapid leaf drying after rain.

12.name: Grape Esca (Black Measles)
12.description: Complex fungal trunk disease causing sudden apoplexy and foliar tiger-striping.

solution.immediate_action: Mark infected vines with tiger-stripe leaves for targeted dormant pruning; sanitize pruning tools.
solution.organic: Apply Trichoderma atroviride pruning wound protectants immediately following trimming.
solution.chemical: Treat pruning wounds with commercial wound sealants containing Thiophanate-methyl.
solution.cultural: Prune in late winter during dry weather; avoid making large pruning cuts on old cordon wood.

13.name: Grape Leaf Blight
13.description: Foliar fungal infection caused by Pseudocercospora cladosporioides.

solution.immediate_action: Prune out dead leaf matter and thin canopy foliage to enhance air movement.
solution.organic: Spray copper hydroxide or potassium silicate formulations.
solution.chemical: Apply Mancozeb, Copper Oxychloride, or Strobilurin fungicides as per local vineyard schedule.
solution.cultural: Collect and burn fallen leaves post-harvest to eliminate overwintering fungal inocula.

14.name: Grape Healthy
14.description: Healthy grape foliage ensuring optimal sugar accumulation in clusters.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Maintain balanced compost tea applications and mycorrhizal root inoculants.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Perform routine canopy leaf pulling around grape clusters to maximize airflow.

15.name: Citrus Greening (Huanglongbing)
15.description: Devastating bacterial disease spread by the Asian citrus psyllid, leading to tree decline.

solution.immediate_action: Quarantine suspected trees; test for Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus and control psyllids.
solution.organic: Release predatory Tamarixia radiata wasps; apply horticultural mineral oils against nymphs.
solution.chemical: Apply Imidacloprid, Thiamethoxam, or Clothianidin systemic insecticides to eliminate Asian citrus psyllid.
solution.cultural: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock; remove and eradicate declining infected trees.

16.name: Peach Bacterial Spot
16.description: Bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni affecting leaves and fruit.

solution.immediate_action: Spray copper bactericide during early morning when temperatures are moderate.
solution.organic: Apply fixed copper combined with Bacillus subtilis during dormancy and petal fall.
solution.chemical: Apply Oxytetracycline (where registered) or copper hydroxide at tight cluster stage.
solution.cultural: Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization; plant windbreaks to minimize leaf abrasion from wind.

17.name: Peach Healthy
17.description: Healthy peach foliage supporting high fruit quality and yield.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Maintain balanced organic mulches and foliar calcium sprays for strong cell walls.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Conduct regular canopy thinning to ensure sunlight reaches interior fruiting wood.

18.name: Bell Pepper Bacterial Spot
18.description: Caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria, severely impacting pepper yields.

solution.immediate_action: Remove and isolate severely spotted pepper plants; eliminate overhead splashing.
solution.organic: Apply copper soap or Streptomyces-based bio-fungicides every 7 days during warm, rainy periods.
solution.chemical: Spray copper hydroxide mixed with Mancozeb to overcome bacterial copper resistance.
solution.cultural: Use certified disease-free seed; practice 3-year crop rotation avoiding Solanaceous plants.

19.name: Bell Pepper Healthy
19.description: Healthy pepper plant foliage with strong disease resistance.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Maintain balanced organic NPK nutrition and foliar kelp extract.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Maintain drip irrigation and plastic mulch to prevent soil-borne pathogen splash.

20.name: Potato Early Blight
20.description: Fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani affecting older leaves first and reducing tuber bulking.

solution.immediate_action: Prune lower diseased potato leaves showing concentric target spots.
solution.organic: Spray copper-based fungicides or bio-fungicide Bacillus amyloliquefaciens on lower leaves.
solution.chemical: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Azoxystrobin on a 7-14 day preventive schedule.
solution.cultural: Implement drip irrigation; maintain plant spacing for air circulation; avoid water stress.

21.name: Potato Late Blight
21.description: Catastrophic oomycete disease caused by Phytophthora infestans requiring rapid fungicide protection.

solution.immediate_action: CRITICAL: Destroy heavily blighted potato foliage immediately to stop airborne zoospore epidemic.
solution.organic: Apply preventative copper hydroxide sprays before high-humidity rain fronts.
solution.chemical: Apply systemic fungicides such as Metalaxyl, Cymoxanil, Dimethomorph, or Mandipropamid with Mancozeb.
solution.cultural: Plant only certified disease-free seed tubers; eliminate volunteer potato plants; ensure good hilling.

22.name: Potato Healthy
22.description: Healthy potato plants with excellent canopy coverage and zero foliar symptoms.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Apply compost mulches and bio-fertilizers; monitor for aphids and Colorado potato beetles.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Maintain hill soil cover over developing tubers to prevent greening and blight spore wash.

23.name: Raspberry Healthy
23.description: Healthy raspberry foliage ensuring high berry production.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Maintain wood chip mulching and organic potassium sulfate fertilizing.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Prune old fruited floricanes after harvest; maintain well-trellised rows.

24.name: Soybean Healthy
24.description: Healthy soybean foliage optimizing nitrogen fixation and pod development.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Inoculate seed with Bradyrhizobium japonicum; maintain balanced soil phosphorus.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Monitor weekly for defoliating caterpillars and stem borers; maintain clean weed control.

25.name: Squash Powdery Mildew
25.description: Common foliar disease caused by Podosphaera xanthii covering cucurbit foliage.

solution.immediate_action: Remove heavily mildewed older leaves; spray immediately to protect young leaves and squash fruit.
solution.organic: Spray potassium bicarbonate (3g/L), milk solution (1:9 dilution), or neem oil every 5-7 days.
solution.chemical: Apply Myclobutanil, Trifloxystrobin, or Quinoxyfen alternating chemical classes.
solution.cultural: Plant powdery mildew-resistant cucurbit varieties; avoid planting in shady, humid areas.

26.name: Strawberry Leaf Scorch
symptoms: Dark purple to brown leaf spots
26.description: Fungal disease caused by Diplocarpon earlianum reducing runner vitality and fruit size.

solution.immediate_action: Remove older infected strawberry leaves showing purple-bordered necrotic lesions.
solution.organic: Apply copper octanoate or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens foliar sprays during vegetative growth.
solution.chemical: Apply Captan, Thiophanate-methyl, or Myclobutanil at early emergence of spring crown leaves.
solution.cultural: Switch from overhead irrigation to drip tape; renovate beds post-harvest and discard old foliage.

27.name: Strawberry Healthy
27.description: Healthy strawberry canopy primed for abundant fruit yield.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Maintain pine straw or plastic mulch beneath berries to preserve soil moisture.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Maintain runner management and provide adequate calcium during flowering.

28.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
28.description: Caused by Xanthomonas species causing necrotic spotting on leaves and stems.

solution.immediate_action: Remove infected leaves in dry conditions; sterilize hands and pruning tools after handling.
solution.organic: Apply fixed copper formulations combined with Bacillus subtilis preventative sprays.
solution.chemical: Spray copper hydroxide tank-mixed with Mancozeb to counter copper-tolerant bacterial strains.
solution.cultural: Use pathogen-free seeds (hot water treated); avoid working in field when tomato foliage is wet.

29.name: Tomato Early Blight
29.description: Caused by Alternaria linariae spreading upward through the canopy.

solution.immediate_action: Prune bottom 12 inches of foliage to eliminate soil-contact and target-spot lesions.
solution.organic: Spray liquid copper fungicide or potassium bicarbonate; mulch heavily beneath tomato plants.
solution.chemical: Apply Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Difenoconazole at 7-10 day intervals after transplanting.
solution.cultural: Stake or cage tomato vines; practice 3-year rotation away from potato/tomato/eggplant.

30.name: Tomato Late Blight
symptoms: Fuzzy white fungal growth on undersides
30.description: Phytophthora infestans infection capable of destroying entire fields in days in cool wet conditions.

solution.immediate_action: URGENT: Isolate affected plants; inspect stems and fruit for water-soaked dark lesions.
solution.organic: Apply preventative copper sprays prior to rainy spells; destroy infected plants in plastic bags.
solution.chemical: Apply systemic fungicides such as Cymoxanil + Mancozeb, Mandipropamid, or Fluopicolide.
solution.cultural: Never compost late-blight infected vines; plant late blight resistant tomato varieties.

31.name: Tomato Leaf Mold
symptoms: Pale green/yellow spots on upper leaf
31.description: Fungal disease caused by Passalora fulva common in humid greenhouses and polyhouses.

solution.immediate_action: Increase greenhouse/tunnel ventilation immediately to drop relative humidity below 80%.
solution.organic: Apply sulfur sprays or bio-fungicides (Bacillus subtilis) to leaf undersides.
solution.chemical: Apply Chlorothalonil, Copper Hydroxide, or Difenoconazole ensuring full underside coverage.
solution.cultural: Prune dense suckers; run circulation fans; space plants widely in greenhouse setups.

32.name: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders and tan centers
32.description: Caused by Septoria lycopersici, one of the most destructive foliar diseases of tomato.

solution.immediate_action: Strip off lower leaves showing small circular spots with dark margins and gray centers.
solution.organic: Apply copper soap fungicides; mulch with straw or cardboard to stop soil splash.
solution.chemical: Spray Chlorothalonil, Mancozeb, or Pyraclostrobin starting at first sign of lower spots.
solution.cultural: Disinfect tomato stakes with 10% bleach solution between seasons; rotate planting beds.

33.name: Tomato Two-Spotted Spider Mites
33.description: Tetranychus urticae infestation sucking sap and causing rapid leaf desiccation.

solution.immediate_action: Spray leaf undersides with strong water jet or insecticidal soap to knock down mite colonies.
solution.organic: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis); apply neem oil or horticultural oils.
solution.chemical: Apply Abamectin, Bifenazate, or Spiromesifen selective miticides alternating modes of action.
solution.cultural: Keep plants well-watered as drought-stressed tomatoes are highly prone to rapid mite outbreaks.

34.name: Tomato Target Spot
symptoms: Brown pinpoint lesions expanding into target spots
34.description: Caused by Corynespora cassiicola causing circular target-like lesions on foliage and fruit.

solution.immediate_action: Prune out lower diseased foliage displaying concentric target lesions.
solution.organic: Apply bio-fungicides containing Trichoderma or copper sulfate protectants.
solution.chemical: Apply Azoxystrobin, Boscalid, or Chlorothalonil on a 10-day preventive schedule.
solution.cultural: Improve row spacing for rapid morning drying; remove and destroy post-harvest tomato vines.

35.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
35.description: Begomovirus transmitted by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci) leading to severe crop failure.

solution.immediate_action: CRITICAL: Rogue out and destroy stunted, curled plants; implement whitefly vector control.
solution.organic: Install 50-mesh insect netting; deploy yellow sticky traps; spray neem oil or insecticidal soap.
solution.chemical: Apply systemic insecticides such as Imidacloprid, Acetamiprid, or Thiamethoxam against whiteflies.
solution.cultural: Eradicate Solanaceous weed hosts (nightshade) around field margins; grow TYLCV-resistant varieties.

36.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns
36.description: Highly contagious tobamovirus spread mechanically through hands, tools, and seeds.

solution.immediate_action: Remove and destroy virus-infected plants immediately; disinfect hands and tools with 20% milk.
solution.organic: No cure for viral infection; apply neem oil to suppress aphids; plant resistant hybrids.
solution.chemical: No chemical virucides exist. Disinfect all tools and stakes with trisodium phosphate (TSP).
solution.cultural: Strictly prohibit tobacco smoking near tomatoes; wash hands thoroughly before working.

37.name: Tomato Healthy
symptoms: Uniform growth and strong blossom set
37.description: Completely healthy tomato plant with optimal photosynthetic efficiency.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Maintain consistent compost mulching and regular calcium/magnesium foliar feeds.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Prune suckers routinely, maintain drip irrigation, and tie vines securely to supports.

38.name: Wheat Stem Rust
symptoms: Reddish-brown to black elongated pustules on stems and leaves
Ruptured epidermis with dark spore dust
38.description: Destructive fungal disease caused by Puccinia graminis f. sp. tritici damaging stems and leaves.

solution.immediate_action: Scout wheat tillers for reddish-brown pustules; alert regional agricultural extension service.
solution.organic: Apply bio-control Trichoderma formulations and preventative copper sprays.
solution.chemical: Apply Triazole fungicides (Propiconazole, Tebuconazole) immediately at flag leaf emergence.
solution.cultural: Plant stem rust-resistant wheat varieties (Sr genes); eradicate alternate host barberry bushes.

39.name: Wheat Stripe Rust
symptoms: Yellow-orange powdery stripes along leaf veins
39.description: Caused by Puccinia striiformis, thriving in cool, humid climates and decimating wheat grain yields.

solution.immediate_action: Inspect leaf blades for yellow-orange linear stripes of rust pustules in cool weather.
solution.organic: Apply sulfur dust or bio-fungicide sprays at early tillering.
solution.chemical: Spray Propiconazole or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole when flag leaf is threatened.
solution.cultural: Sow early-maturing resistant wheat varieties; avoid late nitrogen over-fertilization.

40.name: Wheat Leaf Rust
symptoms: Small circular to oval bright orange pustules
Scattered randomly across upper leaf surfaces
40.description: Caused by Puccinia triticina, the most common rust of wheat worldwide.

solution.immediate_action: Scout upper leaves for small circular orange-brown pustules.
solution.organic: Apply preventative sulfur or botanical neem formulations.
solution.chemical: Apply Tebuconazole, Metconazole, or Pyraclostrobin at flag leaf extension stage.
solution.cultural: Plant diverse multi-line resistant wheat cultivars; ensure balanced potassium nutrition.

41.name: Wheat Powdery Mildew
symptoms: White to grayish cottony patches on leaves and stems
Black speck cleistothecia in mature mats
41.description: Caused by Blumeria graminis f. sp. tritici, reducing photosynthetic surface area in dense stands.

solution.immediate_action: Inspect lower tillers for powdery white mycelial cushions; assess canopy density.
solution.organic: Apply sulfur-based fungicides or potassium bicarbonate in early spring.
solution.chemical: Apply Epoxiconazole, Fenpropimorph, or Prothioconazole at stem elongation stage.
solution.cultural: Avoid dense seed rates; reduce excessive spring nitrogen fertilizer applications.

42.name: Wheat Leaf Blight
symptoms: Tan to brown necrotic spots with chlorotic halos
42.description: Caused by Zymoseptoria tritici and Bipolaris sorokiniana affecting flag leaves.

solution.immediate_action: Check flag leaves for tan necrotic spots with chlorotic yellow borders.
solution.organic: Apply copper oxychloride and bio-fungicides containing Bacillus subtilis.
solution.chemical: Apply Azoxystrobin + Propiconazole or Chlorothalonil at boot stage to protect flag leaf.
solution.cultural: Practice minimum 2-year crop rotation; practice stubble management to bury fungal fruiting bodies.

43.name: Wheat Healthy
43.description: Optimal healthy wheat canopy ready for robust heading and grain filling.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Maintain balanced nitrogen top-dressing and bio-fertilizer seed inoculation.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Maintain optimal seed bed moisture and monitor regularly for weed competition.

44.name: Rice Blast
symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with gray-white centers and brown margins
44.description: Caused by Magnaporthe oryzae, the most devastating fungal disease of cultivated rice worldwide.

solution.immediate_action: Drain paddy field temporarily to reduce relative humidity; avoid excessive nitrogen.
solution.organic: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens or Trichoderma viride seed and foliar treatments.
solution.chemical: Apply Tricyclazole, Isoprothiolane, or Kasugamycin at panicle initiation and heading.
solution.cultural: Plant blast-resistant paddy varieties; practice balanced potassium and silicon fertilization.

45.name: Rice Brown Spot
symptoms: Small circular to oval brown spots with yellowish halo
45.description: Caused by Bipolaris oryzae, historically associated with severe famine in nutrient-deficient soils.

solution.immediate_action: Apply foliar potassium and silicon fertilizer to strengthen silica cell walls.
solution.organic: Spray neem-based formulations and apply bio-control agents at tillering.
solution.chemical: Apply Mancozeb, Propiconazole, or Edifenphos at early symptom appearance.
solution.cultural: Correct soil nutrient deficiencies (especially N, K, and Zn); use clean, certified seed.

46.name: Rice Bacterial Leaf Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked to yellowish wavy stripes along leaf margins
Bacterial ooze droplets in high humidity
46.description: Severe vascular disease caused by Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae causing extensive lodging and grain loss.

solution.immediate_action: Lower water levels in paddy; withhold nitrogen fertilizer until bacterial disease stabilizes.
solution.organic: Spray fresh cow dung slurry extract (bio-antagonist) or Streptomyces-based formulations.
solution.chemical: Apply Copper Hydroxide mixed with Streptocycline (plant antibiotic where approved).
solution.cultural: Avoid clipping rice seedling tips during transplanting; maintain clean bunds free of weed hosts.

47.name: Rice Sheath Blight
symptoms: Oval greenish-gray water-soaked lesions on leaf sheaths
47.description: Fungal disease caused by Rhizoctonia solani spreading rapidly in warm, dense flooded paddies.

solution.immediate_action: Drain excess standing water; clear floating organic debris from paddy surface.
solution.organic: Apply Trichoderma harzianum or Bacillus subtilis to water line and base of tillers.
solution.chemical: Apply Validamycin, Hexaconazole, or Thifluzamide targeting the lower stem sheath zone.
solution.cultural: Adopt wider hill spacing (20x15 cm) to improve light penetration; avoid excessive nitrogen.

48.name: Rice Healthy
48.description: Healthy rice crop foliage with optimal photosynthetic rate and tiller development.

solution.immediate_action: Crop is healthy. No intervention required.
solution.organic: Apply Azolla green manure and beneficial blue-green algae bio-fertilizers.
solution.chemical: No chemical applications needed.
solution.cultural: Maintain Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) irrigation to encourage deep root growth.
